knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem and the Rank-Nullity Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $\text{Null}(A)=\{\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ -9{x}_{1} \\ -4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}?$ 

I. $\text{rank}(A)=3$

II. $\text{Col}(A)={R}^{4}$

III. $A$ is not invertible
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible

$\,⇔\,\left\{\begin{aligned}\text{Col}(A) &={R}^{4} \\ \text{dim(Col}(A)) &=4=\text{rank}(A) \\ \text{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \text{dim(Null}(A)) &=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ -9 \\ -4\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=1.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

$$
\text{rank}(A)+1=4,\qquad \text{rank}(A)=4-1=3.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=3$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=1$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 3. The number of pivot columns is 3, and the number of non-pivot columns is 1.

- Statement I is true. $\text{rank}(A)=3$.

- Statement II is false. The column-space dimension is 3, less than 4.

- Statement III is true. The rank is less than the number of columns.

Therefore, the correct answer is I and III only.

$$

I. The number of non-pivot columns in $A$ is equal to $3$

III. $\text{rank}(A)=2$

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}15 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\;\begin{bmatrix}9 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=2.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

$$

- Statement II is false. The column-space dimension is 2, less than 4.

- Statement III is true. $\text{rank}(A)=2$.

Therefore, the correct answer is III only.

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\text{Span}\left\{\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\right\}?
$$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible

$$
\Longleftrightarrow\quad\left\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Col}(A) &=\mathbb{R}^{4} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Col}(A)) &=4=\operatorname{rank}(A) \\ \operatorname{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) &=0=\operatorname{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -3 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=1.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

$$
\text{rank}(A)+1=4,\qquad \text{rank}(A)=4-1=3.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=3$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=1$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 3. The number of pivot columns is 3, and the number of non-pivot columns is 1.

- Statement “$\text{Col}(A)={R}^{4}$” is false. The column-space dimension is 3, less than 4.

- Statement “$\text{rank}(A)=2$” is false. $\text{rank}(A)=3$.

- Statement “The number of non-pivot columns in $A$ is equal to $1$” is true. The number of non-pivot columns is 1.

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $\text{Null}(A)=\left\{\begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 6{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{3} \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R\right\}?$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible

$$
\Longleftrightarrow\quad\left\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Col}(A) &=\mathbb{R}^{4} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Col}(A)) &=4=\operatorname{rank}(A) \\ \operatorname{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) &=0=\operatorname{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\;\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 6 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\;\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=3.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

$$
\text{rank}(A)+3=4,\qquad \text{rank}(A)=4-3=1.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=1$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=3$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 1. The number of pivot columns is 1, and the number of non-pivot columns is 3.

- Statement “$A$ is invertible” is false. The rank is less than the number of columns.

- Statement “$\text{Col}(A)$ is a $1$-dimensional subspace of ${R}^{4}$” is true. $\dim(\text{Col}(A))=1$.

- Statement “$\text{rank}(A)=1$” is true. $\text{rank}(A)=1$.

Therefore, the correct answer is $\text{Col}(A)$ is a $1$-dimensional subspace of ${R}^{4}$; $\text{rank}(A)=1$.
